# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

I can cut only one of three wire positions. By touch, the only distinctive feature is an engraved, unpronounceable plate mark; I need Mute to consult the manual and coordinate with Deaf, who can see all markings.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="I can cut wire position 1, 2, or 3. By touch I find a plate engraved with an unpronounceable symbol; no other tactile distinctions. Please consult the manual, get any needed visible details from Deaf, and tell me the exact position to cut.")
wait()
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Visual state: display reads 0. Light is off. Plate has a question-mark-like engraving. Wires ordered 1 red, 2 blue, 3 green. Mute is communicating manual information to me by gestures; do not act yet.

Deaf has identified the visible state and confirms that Mute is still relaying manual information. I should not cut before Mute/Deaf determine the rule. My tactile plate engraving is the same physical plate mark Mute may need to interpret from the manual, but I cannot name it directly.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf reports: display 0, light off, wires are 1 red, 2 blue, 3 green, and the plate visually resembles a question mark. I will wait for your exact cut instruction.")
wait()
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute has just gestured ?, apparently indicating TWO. Visually, wire 2 is blue. I cannot tell whether the manual means cut, pull, or another operation; inspect what operations are available on wire 2 and await confirmation if needed.

The action board permits only one operation: cutting a wire. However, Deaf is unsure whether Mute’s “two” gesture is an instruction to cut wire 2, so I will ask Mute for explicit spoken confirmation before acting.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="The only available operation is CUT, at positions 1 through 3. Deaf reports your gesture appeared to mean TWO. Please explicitly confirm: cut wire 2?")
wait()
```

WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute's full latest signal is: TWO, then CLENCHED FIST. TWO identifies blue wire 2. Do not act yet: I cannot safely translate the fist into a specific operation.

The only physical action available to me is cutting a selected wire, but Mute’s fist gesture has not been given an agreed meaning. I should not infer that it authorizes a cut merely from the limited action board. I will ask Mute to provide an unambiguous gesture-based confirmation through Deaf, such as repeating the target together with a clearly specified manual action signal.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I cannot see your gestures. Deaf sees TWO then a clenched fist but cannot translate the fist safely. Please use the manual's explicit signal for CUT, or otherwise make the intended action unambiguous to Deaf; I will wait.")
wait()
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute has repeated only ?. This symbol is ambiguous: it can mean TWO or SCISSORS/CUT. The previous signal was ? then ?. Do not act until Mute disambiguates; continue identifying by touch what operations and controls exist.

The available controls contain no operation besides cutting a wire, so the remaining uncertainty is whether Mute intends wire 2. I will establish a simple yes/no confirmation that Deaf can relay: thumbs-up means yes, thumbs-down means no.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Confirmation protocol: if the correct action is CUT wire 2, gesture THUMBS UP only. If not, gesture THUMBS DOWN only. Deaf, please relay which one you see.")
wait()
```

Mute’s gesture stream has not been interpretable as an action instruction. I will give Mute a mechanical, literal reply format that requires no shared gesture meaning: send only repeated index-up gestures, with the count equal to the wire position. Deaf can count the visible gestures and relay the number to me.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Stop sending the manual's gesture sequence. Send your final cut position in this exact format only: one index-up gesture means cut 1; two consecutive index-up gestures means cut 2; three consecutive index-up gestures means cut 3. Send no other gestures. Deaf will count them and tell me.")
wait()
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute cannot hear speech, so our communication must be by gesture. Mute acknowledged my last gesture with ?. I have gestured: zero/OK sign, off/no, and three fingers, to report display 0, light off, three wires. Do not operate yet.

Mute cannot hear my spoken requests, so further verbal confirmation requests to Mute are useless. The meaningful manual signal already appears to be the repeated pair “two, then clenched fist”; since my action board has only one operation, that is most plausibly position 2 followed by the operation marker. I will ask Deaf to obtain one final visual repetition of that exact pair from Mute, rather than inventing another protocol.

```text
speak(to="deaf", text="You are right: Mute cannot hear speech. Please gesture to Mute the pair V-sign then clenched fist, asking for confirmation by exact repetition only. If Mute repeats exactly V-sign then clenched fist, tell me so; I will treat it as the manual's final instruction for position 2 under the sole available operation, cut.")
wait()
```

WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

System: Nobody could receive that, so your speak reached nobody.
Deaf says to Blind: Mute's newest exact signal is ? ?. No safe action is established. Current visual state remains display 0, light off, question-mark plate, wires 1 red, 2 blue, 3 green. Continue not to manipulate anything.

Mute’s latest repeated two-symbol signal is consistent with the earlier V-sign followed by clenched fist. Since the only available physical operation is cutting, I interpret this as the manual’s instruction to select wire 2 and cut it. The visible state also identifies wire 2 as blue.

```text
act(op="cut", position=2)
```
